what_it_does: A humectant and skin-conditioning ingredient that helps soothe and support the skin barrier.
summary_short: Panthenol, also called provitamin B5, is used to hydrate, soften, and calm the skin. It is especially common in sensitive-skin and barrier-support formulas, where it may help reduce tightness, redness, and discomfort.
summary_long:
Panthenol is a water-soluble form of provitamin B5 used in skincare as a humectant and skin-conditioning ingredient. In formulas, it helps attract and hold water in the outer skin layers, which can make skin feel softer, smoother, and less tight.

Its main skincare role is barrier support and soothing. Panthenol is often included in sensitive-skin products because hydrated, better-functioning barrier skin is less prone to stinging, dryness, and visible irritation. A review of sensitive-skin products found panthenol among the ingredients with volunteer-based study support in people with sensitive skin [PMID:unknown].

Clinical evidence for panthenol itself is moderate but not standalone in most of the provided studies. A 2025 observational study tested a cream containing Centella asiatica leaf extract, ceramide NP, and panthenol in women with sensitive skin. After 2–4 weeks, participants had lower sensitive-skin symptom scores, reduced redness, lower transepidermal water loss, and higher skin hydration, with only mild, self-limiting adverse events [PMID:unknown]. Because the product combined multiple barrier-support ingredients, the results support panthenol’s use in this type of formula, but do not prove it was the only active ingredient responsible.

Panthenol also appears in scalp and hair-care products. In a 24-week randomized, double-blind study, a regimen containing panthenol plus other ingredients such as niacinamide, caffeine, and anti-dandruff agents reduced hair shedding and improved scalp barrier measurements compared with placebo [PMID:unknown]. For consumers, this is most relevant to scalp-care formulas, not as proof that panthenol alone treats hair loss.

Panthenol is generally considered gentle and is commonly paired with barrier and calming ingredients such as ceramides, niacinamide, allantoin, Centella asiatica, and glycerin. No major routine conflicts are suggested by the provided evidence, and it can fit into both morning and evening routines, including alongside exfoliants or retinoids when extra barrier support is helpful.
